bull_case: The combination can create a rare end-to-end stack from component design through recurring space applications.
bear_case: Neutron execution, government concentration and integration complexity can prevent breadth from becoming durable leadership.
thesis: Rocket Lab has become a structural leader among non-SpaceX commercial space platforms. Its strategic position spans launch, satellite buses/components, defense payloads, optical systems and—if Iridium closes—recurring communications/PNT services.

evidence.claim: FY2025 revenue was $601.8M with Launch Services $199.0M and Space Systems $402.8M.
Iridium adds recurring communications/PNT applications and a global network.

counterevidence: Rocket Lab remains cash-flow negative on a standalone basis and the Iridium transaction materially increases integration, financing and dilution complexity.
unknowns: Neutron commercial readiness and launch economics
Long-run dilution cadence and owner FCF/share conversion
falsifiers: A major Neutron delay, persistent launch failures, failure to close/integrate Iridium, or continued double-digit share dilution without per-share FCF progress would weaken the thesis.
next_checks: Neutron schedule, backlog conversion, post-close Iridium FCF, diluted share count, ATM usage

subscores.rationale: Government/defense, communications, PNT, Earth observation and responsive launch support multi-year space-infrastructure demand.
Rocket Lab is one of the few commercial operators with regular orbital launch, spacecraft manufacturing and now a path to owned satellite applications.
Multiple independent demand axes reduce reliance on a single launch product, especially after Iridium.

uncertainties.rationale: Rocket Lab remains in a high-investment, acquisition-heavy transition with large execution variance.
